newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Nutreco places shares, converts loans.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Nutreco places shares, converts loans.

text.p: Dutch unlisted animal and fish feeds group Nutreco Holding NV said on Wednesday it had raised 150 million guilders through a private placement of cumulative preference shares.
Nutreco, which emerged in 1994 from a $425 million management buy-out of British Petroleum's nutrition unit, said the stock was bought by five Dutch financial institutions.

The proceeds were used to redeem part of the long-term loans taken up at the time of the management buy-out. The 122 million guilders remaining of the shareholder loans have been converted into another class of cumulative preference shares, it said.

The company added the transactions had strengthened its balance sheet with a total of 272 million guilders of new equity which reduced its gearing and cut annual capital cost by five million guilders.
Nutreco's assets total 1.5 billion guilders and it expects 1996 sales of 4.5 billion. Last year it posted turnover of just above four billion guilders and net profit of 26 million.
